title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Ten Typical Cases of Expropriation and Demolition by People's Courts
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Release of Ten Typical Cases on People's Courts' Expropriation and Demolition

I. Yang Ruifen v. Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government — Dispute over Housing Expropriation Decision

(1) Basic Facts

On October 16, 2007, the Zhuzhou Real Estate Administration issued a House Relocation Permit (Zhu Fang Chai Qian Zi [2007] No. 19) to Hunan Metallurgical Vocational and Technical College. Part of Yang Ruifen's house fell within the demolition scope but was not demolished within the permitted period. In 2010, the Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government initiated the Shennong Avenue construction project. On July 25, 2010, the Zhuzhou Development and Reform Commission approved the project. On July 14, 2011, the Zhuzhou Planning Bureau issued a Construction Land Planning Permit (Zhu Gui Yong [2011] No. 0066). Yang Ruifen's house was located at the intersection of Taishan Road and the planned Shennong Avenue, covering an area of 418 m², with a building area of 582.12 m². The ground level of the house was over 10 meters higher than that of Shennong Avenue. Part of the house fell within the red-line boundary of the Shennong Avenue construction project. On July 15, 2011, after deliberation, the Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government published the "Compensation Plan for Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land for the Shennong Avenue Project" to solicit public opinions. On September 15, 2011, a social stability risk assessment rated it as Level C. On September 30, 2011, the Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government released a revised compensation plan and issued the "Decision on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land of Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government" (Zhu Zheng [2011] No. 1) (hereinafter "Expropriation Decision"), expropriating Yang Ruifen's entire building and providing reasonable compensation.

Yang Ruifen disagreed, arguing that "the applicant's house was within the demolition scope of the new campus project of Hunan Metallurgical Vocational and Technical College under a valid relocation permit, and the respondent's expropriation decision conflicts with the previously effective house relocation permit" and that "neither the original project demolition party nor the respondent provided a reasonable resettlement and compensation plan for the applicant." She applied to the Hunan Provincial People's Government for administrative reconsideration. The reconsideration authority held that the House Relocation Permit originally obtained by Hunan Metallurgical Vocational and Technical College had expired, and the respondent's expropriation of the applicant's house under the "Regulation on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" did not violate the law. Part of the applicant's house was within the red-line boundary of the Shennong Avenue project, and the ground level of the house was over 10 meters higher than that of Shennong Avenue. Failure to demolish the entire house would pose serious safety hazards, making it necessary to demolish it. The Expropriation Decision was appropriate in content and had complied with relevant legal procedures before issuance. Therefore, the reconsideration authority upheld the Expropriation Decision. Yang Ruifen then filed an administrative lawsuit against the Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government, seeking to revoke the Expropriation Decision.

(2) Judgment

The Tianyuan District People's Court of Zhuzhou City held at first instance that, regarding Yang Ruifen's argument that the Expropriation Decision (Zhu Zheng [2011] No. 1) conflicted with the House Relocation Permit (Zhu Fang Chai Qian Zi [2007] No. 19) in terms of subject and content, since Permit No. [2007] No. 19 had already expired and the Shennong Avenue project was a new project, there was no conflict between the two documents. Regarding Yang Ruifen's claim that expropriating her house outside the red-line boundary was unlawful, because part of her house was within the red-line boundary of the Shennong Avenue project, the expropriation was for public interest needs, and the house's ground level was over 10 meters higher than that of Shennong Avenue; failure to demolish the entire building would create serious safety hazards, and a complete expropriation and demolition was practical. Yang Ruifen argued that the Shennong Avenue construction project had not obtained a Construction Land Approval Certificate. On July 14, 2011, the Zhuzhou Planning Bureau issued a Construction Land Planning Permit (Zhu Gui Yong [2011] No. 0066) for the Shennong Avenue project. Yang Ruifen contended that the explanation provided by the Zhuzhou Planning Bureau during the reconsideration proceedings could not serve as a basis for expropriation beyond the scope. The explanation issued by the Zhuzhou Planning Bureau during reconsideration was a separate legal relationship and not within the scope of trial in this case. The Expropriation Decision of the Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government was based on clear facts, lawful procedures, and correct application of laws and regulations. The court upheld the decision.

The Zhuzhou Intermediate People's Court at second instance held that the key issue was whether the Expropriation Decision (Zhu Zheng [2011] No. 1) was lawful. In 2010, the Zhuzhou Municipal People's Government initiated the Shennong Avenue construction project. On July 14, 2011, the Zhuzhou Planning Bureau issued the Construction Land Planning Permit (Zhu Gui Yong [2011] No. 0066). Part of Yang Ruifen's house was within the red-line boundary of the Shennong Avenue project. Although expropriating Yang Ruifen's entire building exceeded the special plan for Shennong Avenue, the expropriation was for public interest needs, and the house's ground level was over 10 meters higher than that of Shennong Avenue. If only the part of the house within the planning red-line boundary were demolished, the remaining part outside the boundary would artificially become a dangerous building, losing its value and function. Expropriating the entire building of Yang Ruifen and providing reasonable compensation was consistent with the actual situation and reflected the people's government's responsibility for the safety of people's lives and property. The appeal was dismissed, and the first-instance judgment was affirmed.

(3) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case lies in: during the process of house expropriation, if due to unreasonable planning, a part of an entire building is not included within the planning red-line boundary, the government, considering factors such as practicality and residential safety, may expropriate the unincluded part together. This action reflects a people-oriented approach and facilitates the smooth progress of expropriation work. The people's court recognizes the legality of such an expropriation decision and does not endorse an overly rigid or mechanical interpretation of the law.

II. Kong Qingfeng v. Sishui County People's Government — Dispute over Housing Expropriation Decision

(1) Basic Facts

On April 6, 2011, the Sishui County People's Government issued the "Decision on Implementing House Expropriation in the Forestry Bureau Area East of Sihe Road and the Area North of Gucheng Road West of Sihe Road in Sicheng" (Si Zheng Fa [2011] No. 15) (hereinafter "Decision"). The compensation plan stipulated that for those choosing monetary compensation, the main expropriated house would be compensated at the preferential price of multi-story property rights exchange resettlement houses in the same block; for those choosing property rights exchange, the portion of the resettlement house exceeding the compensated area of the main house would be paid by the person whose house is expropriated, with the portion within 10 square meters settled at the preferential price, and the portion exceeding 10 square meters settled at the market price; for the portion where the area of the expropriated main house exceeds the resettlement house area, monetary compensation would be given at the preferential price for resettlement houses plus 300 yuan/m². The plaintiff, Kong Qingfeng, had his house within the expropriation scope and, disagreeing with the Decision, filed an administrative lawsuit.

(2) Judgment

The Jining Intermediate People's Court held after trial that, according to Articles 2 and 19 of the "Regulation on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land" (hereinafter "Regulation"), when expropriating houses on state-owned land owned by units or individuals, fair compensation shall be given to the owners of the expropriated houses. The compensation for the value of the expropriated house shall not be lower than the market price of similar real estate on the date the expropriation decision is announced. According to the legislative spirit, compensation for the expropriated house should refer to the price of new commercial housing in a nearby location, ensuring that the living conditions and quality of life of the person whose house is expropriated are not reduced after expropriation. In this case, the preferential price was clearly lower than the market price, and the compensation price for the expropriated house was also significantly lower than the purchase price paid by the person whose house is expropriated. The provisions of this expropriation compensation plan were manifestly unfair to the person whose house is expropriated and violated the relevant provisions of the Regulation. Therefore, the court ruled to revoke the Decision made by the defendant, Sishui County People's Government. After the judgment, none of the parties appealed.

(3) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case lies in: the principle of fair compensation to the person whose house is expropriated, as stipulated in Article 2 of the "Regulation on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land," should run through the entire process of house expropriation and compensation. Whether in litigation concerning expropriation decisions or compensation decisions, the people's court must adhere to a combination of procedural and substantive review. Once it is found that the compensation standard determined by the compensation plan is clearly lower than the statutory "market price of similar real estate," even if the expropriation decision affects a large area or involves a large number of people, the court must resolutely confirm its illegality or revoke it if necessary, to effectively safeguard the fundamental rights and interests of the people.

III. He Gang v. Huaiyin District People's Government of Huai'an City — Dispute over Housing Expropriation Compensation Decision

(1) Basic Facts

On October 29, 2011, the Huaiyin District People's Government of Huai'an City (hereinafter "Huaiyin District Government") issued an "Announcement on the Decision to Expropriate Houses," deciding to expropriate houses and ancillary facilities within the planning red-line boundary of the Yinchuan Road East Old City Reconstruction Project. On the same day, the Huaiyin District Government issued the "Compensation Plan for House Expropriation in the Yinchuan Road East Block." He Gang's house, located at No. 205, Building 3, North Side of Huanghe Road, Huaiyin District, Huai'an City, fell within the above expropriation scope. After appraisal, the unit price for the residential portion of He Gang's expropriated house was RMB 3,901 per square meter, and the unit price for the commercial portion was RMB 15,600 per square meter. During the negotiation process for expropriation compensation, He Gang indicated to the expropriation department his choice of property rights exchange, but the two parties failed to reach an agreement on the location and area of the property rights exchange. On June 14, 2012, the Huaiyin District Government, upon application by the expropriation department, issued the "Decision on House Expropriation Compensation" (Huai Zheng Fang Zheng Bu Jue Zi [2012] No. 01), which mainly stated: He Gang's expropriated house had a building area of 59.04 square meters, with a designed use of commercial-residential. Because the two parties failed to reach a compensation agreement within the signing period determined in the expropriation compensation plan, the Huaiyin District Government made the expropriation compensation decision: 1. The total monetary compensation for the person whose house is expropriated was RMB 607,027.15; 2. He Gang, the person whose house is expropriated, was to complete relocation within 7 days from the date of receipt of this decision. He Gang disagreed and applied to the Huai'an Municipal People's Government for administrative reconsideration, which subsequently upheld the expropriation compensation decision. He Gang still disagreed and filed an administrative lawsuit with the court, requesting the revocation of the expropriation compensation decision made by the Huaiyin District Government.

(2) Judgment

The Huaiyin District People's Court of Huai'an City held that the focus of the dispute was whether the sued house expropriation compensation decision infringed upon He Gang's right to choose the compensation method. According to Article 21, paragraph 1, of the Regulation, a person whose house is expropriated may choose monetary compensation or property rights exchange. Through analysis of the evidence in this case, it could be determined that He Gang had chosen property rights exchange as the compensation method, but the compensation decision in question determined monetary compensation, thereby infringing upon He Gang's right to choose compensation. Accordingly, the court ruled to revoke the sued compensation decision. After the first-instance judgment, neither party appealed.

(3) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case lies in: in litigation over house compensation decisions, it clearly upholds the right of the person whose house is expropriated to choose the compensation method. Article 21 of the Regulation clearly stipulates: "The person whose house is expropriated may choose monetary compensation or property rights exchange for the house." In practice, many conflicts between the government and the people arise because city or county governments, when making compensation decisions, do not give the person whose house is expropriated the opportunity to choose the compensation method and directly determine it. The revocation judgment in this case fundamentally corrected this typical illegal act by administrative organs, providing adequate judicial relief for the parties.

IV. Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang v. Yushan District People's Government of Ma'anshan City — Dispute over Housing Expropriation Compensation Decision

(1) Basic Facts

On March 20, 2012, the Yushan District People's Government issued the "Yushan District People's Government Expropriation Decision" (Yu Cheng Zheng [2012] No. 2) and the "Announcement on House Expropriation for the Caishi Ancient Town Old City Reconstruction Project." The house owned by Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang, located at No. 22, Caishi Jiuhua Street, Yushan District, Ma'anshan City, fell within the expropriation scope. The property certificate recorded a building area of 774.59 square meters; property type: private; designed use: commercial. The land certificate recorded a use area of 1,185.9 square meters; land category (use): comprehensive; use type: transfer. In December 2012, under the full witnessing and supervision of judicial personnel, the Yushan District house expropriation department selected by lottery the real estate price appraisal agency for the house at No. 22, Caishi Jiuhua Street, which was Anhui Minsheng Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. On December 12, 2012, Anhui Minsheng Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. submitted a market value appraisal report for the house owned by Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang to the Yushan District house expropriation department. On January 16, 2013, the Yushan District People's Government issued the "Decision on House Expropriation Compensation" (Yu Zheng Zheng Bu [2013] No. 21) to Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang, the persons whose houses were expropriated. Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang argued that the defendant did not serve the house appraisal result to the plaintiffs before making the compensation decision, depriving them of their legally entitled rights. Therefore, they filed an administrative lawsuit, requesting the revocation of the "Decision on House Expropriation Compensation."

(2) Judgment

The Ma'anshan Intermediate People's Court held that, according to Article 19 of the Regulation, the value of the expropriated house shall be determined by a real estate price appraisal agency in accordance with the house expropriation appraisal method. If a person has objections to the appraised value of the expropriated house, they may apply to the real estate price appraisal agency for a review appraisal. If they have objections to the review result, they may apply to the real estate price appraisal expert committee for appraisal. According to Articles 16, 17, 20, and 22 of the "Measures for Appraisal of Houses Expropriated on State-owned Land" issued by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the house expropriation department shall publicize the preliminary individual household appraisal results within the expropriation scope to the persons whose houses are expropriated. After the publicity period expires, the house expropriation department shall deliver the individual household appraisal report to the persons whose houses are expropriated. If a person whose house is expropriated objects to the appraisal result, they may, within 10 days of receiving the appraisal report, apply to the real estate appraisal agency for a review appraisal. If they object to the review result, they may, within 10 days of receiving the review result, apply to the real estate price appraisal expert committee for appraisal. Based on the existing evidence in this case, after Anhui Minsheng Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued the market value appraisal report for the commercial real estate at No. 22, Caishi Jiuhua Street, the Yushan District house expropriation department failed to timely deliver the report's content to Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang and to publicize it, thereby causing Ai Zhengyun and Sha Defang to lose their rights to apply for a review appraisal and to apply to the real estate price appraisal expert committee for appraisal regarding the appraisal price of their property. This constituted a violation of legal procedures. Accordingly, the court ruled to revoke the "Decision on House Expropriation Compensation" (Yu Zheng Zheng Bu [2013] No. 21) issued by the Yushan District People's Government. After the judgment was announced, none of the parties appealed.

(3) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case lies in: through strict procedural review, focusing on the detail of whether the appraisal report was served, it demonstrates the judiciary's comprehensive protection of the right to fair compensation for persons whose houses are expropriated. The house value appraisal report is one of the most important bases for administrative organs to make compensation decisions. If the appraisal report is not served in a timely manner, it will prevent the person whose house is expropriated from exercising their statutory rights to apply for review and appraisal, thereby causing the compensation decision itself to lose its legal basis. This judgment keenly grasped the important connection between procedural issues and the protection of substantive rights, resolutely revoked the compensation decision, and provided adequate and thorough protection.

V. Wen Baian v. Shangcheng County People's Government — Dispute over Housing Expropriation Compensation Decision

(1) Basic Facts

Most of the houses in the Yingchuntai area of Shangcheng County town were built over 30 years ago, severely damaged, and had poor infrastructure. On December 8, 2012, the Shangcheng County house expropriation department issued the "Announcement on the Selection of Appraisal Agencies for House Expropriation in Yingchuntai Shantytown Area," listing Xinyang Mingyu Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd., Anhui Zhong'an Real Estate Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd., and Shangcheng County Longsheng Real Estate Appraisal Office as qualified appraisal agencies for selection by the persons whose houses were expropriated. Later, because the expropriator and the persons whose houses were expropriated failed to reach a consensus, the Shangcheng County house expropriation department issued the "Announcement on the Lottery for Appraisal Agencies for House Expropriation in Yingchuntai Shantytown Area" on December 11, and on December 14 organized a lottery with affected persons and public representatives, selecting Xinyang Mingyu Real Estate Appraisers Co., Ltd. as the price appraisal agency for this house expropriation. On December 24, 2012, the Shangcheng County People's Government issued the "Decision on Renovation and Construction of Yingchuntai Resettlement Area and House Expropriation" (Shang Zheng [2012] No. 24). The house of the plaintiff, Wen Baian, at No. 132, Yingchuntai, where he had long resided, fell within the expropriation scope. On May 10, 2013, the real estate price appraisal agency issued a preliminary house appraisal report. The Shangcheng County house expropriation department and the plaintiff failed to reach a compensation agreement within the signing period determined in the expropriation compensation plan. On July 15, 2013, the defendant, based on the house appraisal report, issued the "Decision on House Expropriation Compensation of Shangcheng County People's Government" (Shang Zheng Bu Jue Zi [2013] No. 3). The plaintiff disagreed with the expropriation compensation decision and filed a lawsuit with the people's court.

(2) Judgment

The Xinyang Intermediate People's Court held that the legality of the sued expropriation compensation decision had the following issues: (1) The selection procedure for the appraisal agency was illegal. The Shangcheng County house expropriation department issued the "Announcement on the Selection of Appraisal Agencies for House Expropriation in Yingchuntai Shantytown Area" on December 8, 2012, but the Shangcheng County People's Government did not issue the "Decision on Renovation and Construction of Yingchuntai Resettlement Area and House Expropriation" until December 24, 2012. That is, the announcement for selecting the appraisal agency was made before the house expropriation decision was issued. This did not comply with the provisions of Article 20, paragraph 1, of the Regulation, which states: "The real estate price appraisal agency shall be selected by the persons whose houses are expropriated through negotiation; if negotiation fails, it shall be determined through majority decision, random selection, or other methods, with specific measures formulated by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government," and also violated the provisions of Article 6 of the "Henan Province Provisions on Implementing the Regulation on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land," thus violating legal procedures. (2) The determination of the ownership of plaintiff Wen Baian's house was erroneous. In the "Explanation on the Inconsistency of the Ownership Subject of Wen Baian's House," the defendant stated that "Wen Baian refused to cooperate during the appraisal process, preventing the appraisers from entering the house for inspection," but in the "Investigation and Determination Report on Real Estate Ownership in Yingchuntai Resettlement Area," it stated that "this area is the area measured by the county expropriation office entering the house, and the real estate ownership status is undisputed." The evidence provided by the defendant was contradictory, and there was insufficient evidence to prove that the defendant was unable to perform the inspection procedure due to the plaintiff's reasons. Moreover, the registered obligees on the house ownership certificate and the state-owned land use right certificate were a third person, Wen Ran, not Wen Baian. The defendant's determination of the ownership of the house on the expropriated land was indeed erroneous. Accordingly, the court of first instance ruled to revoke the sued house expropriation compensation decision. After the judgment was announced, none of the parties appealed.

(3) Typical Significance

VI. Huo Peiying v. Huangpu District People's Government of Shanghai — Dispute over Housing Expropriation Compensation Decision

(I) Basic Facts

The premises at No. 283, Lane 281-283 Shunchang Road, Shanghai, Second Floor, Unit 283, was a public rental house leased by the plaintiff, Huo Peiying. The house type was old-style lane, the use was residential, the living area was 11.9 square meters, equivalent to a constructed area of 18.33 square meters. The household had four registered members: Huo Peiying, Sun Weixuan, Chen Weili, and Sun Weiqiang. Due to the need for old city reconstruction, on June 2, 2012, the defendant, Huangpu District People's Government of Shanghai, issued a housing expropriation decision (Huangfu Zheng [2012] No. 2). The plaintiff's residential house was located within the expropriation scope. Because the plaintiff's household claimed that they operated a company and should receive compensation for non-residential housing, the expropriation parties failed to reach an expropriation compensation agreement within the signing period. On April 11, 2013, the housing expropriation department, the third party, Huangpu District Housing Support and Housing Administration Bureau of Shanghai, submitted a report to the defendant requesting the issuance of an expropriation compensation decision. The defendant accepted the case and held a coordination hearing on April 16, 2013, but the coordination failed because the plaintiff's household left the meeting on their own. After reviewing and verifying relevant evidence, the defendant issued Housing Expropriation Compensation Decision (Hu Huangfu Fang Zheng Bu [2013] No. 010) on April 23, 2013. The decision determined that the expropriated house of the plaintiff's household was a residential house, and ordered: 1. The housing expropriation department shall compensate the public housing lessee, Huo Peiying's household, by way of property rights exchange; the property for exchange was located at Room 204, No. 3, Lane 121, Donglan Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai; the Huo Peiying household shall pay the housing expropriation department a price difference of RMB 476,706.84; 2. The housing expropriation department shall pay the Huo Peiying household various subsidies, rewards, etc., totaling RMB 492,150; the relocation fee for household facilities shall be settled according to the actual amount; the sign-and-move reward shall be settled according to the moving date; 3. The Huo Peiying household shall move to the aforementioned property for exchange within 15 days from the date of receiving the housing expropriation compensation decision and vacate the expropriated house.

The plaintiff, dissatisfied with this expropriation compensation decision, applied for administrative reconsideration to the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, which upheld the decision. Still dissatisfied, the plaintiff filed an administrative lawsuit with the Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai, seeking to revoke the contested expropriation compensation decision.

(II) Judgment

The Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai held that the defendant had the administrative authority to make the contested housing expropriation compensation decision; the administrative procedure of the decision was lawful; the applicable laws and regulations were correct; and the decision did not harm the plaintiff's household's legitimate rights and interests. The main dispute in this case was whether the nature of the plaintiff's expropriated house should be classified as residential or non-residential. Upon investigation, the registered addresses of Shanghai Yanglin Jilong Investment Co., Ltd. and Shanghai Jilong Ecological Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd., for which Sun Weixuan served as the legal representative, were both in Jinshan District, Shanghai. Although the business address was registered as No. 281 Shunchang Road, Shanghai, the business terms of the two companies were from December 2003 to December 2008, and the nature of the plaintiff's leased public house was residential. The plaintiff's request that the defendant provide compensation for Sun Weixuan's company operation lacked a legal basis, and the expropriation compensation plan also had no such provision. The contested expropriation compensation decision's compensation to the plaintiff for residential housing had a legal basis. Accordingly, the court of first instance rendered a judgment dismissing the plaintiff's claims. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the parties appealed.

(III) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case is that it provides positive reference for determining whether an expropriated house is a residential house and applying different compensation standards accordingly. In practice, the premise of what people most care about, "according to what standard to compensate," is often "what is the nature and use of the house," leading to many disputes. Courts in practice usually determine the nature of a house based on the use indicated in the property registration certificate. However, if the indicated use is inconsistent with the expropriated person's claim, the expropriated person needs to provide a business license and other relevant evidence to support the claim, only then might the court consider a different compensation standard. In this case, the plaintiff failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that the involved house was non-residential; therefore, the court did not support the claim.

VII. Mao Peirong v. Yongchang County People's Government — Dispute over House Expropriation Compensation Decision

(I) Basic Facts

In January 2012, the Yongchang County People's Government drafted the "Compensation Plan for Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land for the Beihaizi Scenic Area Construction Project in Yongchang County" and solicited public opinions. After the period expired, it issued the "Decision on Expropriation of Houses on State-owned Land for the Beihaizi Scenic Area Construction Project in Yongchang County" and made a public announcement. The plaintiff, Mao Peirong, Liu Jihua, and Mao Xianfeng (husband, wife, and son), co-owned a residential house (area 276 square meters) and an industrial house (area 775.8 square meters), both within the expropriation scope. Upon notice from the housing expropriation department, Mao Peirong and others selected an appraisal agency to appraise the expropriated houses. After the appraisal report was issued, Mao Peirong and others applied for a review on the grounds of omissions. The appraisal agency reviewed and issued a new appraisal report, providing a detailed explanation of the omitted items. On December 26 of the same year, after multiple unsuccessful negotiations with Mao Peirong regarding compensation, the housing expropriation department informed him that if he disagreed with the appraisal review result, he could, in accordance with the "Measures for the Appraisal of Houses Expropriated on State-owned Land," apply for an expert appraisal to the Jinchang City Real Estate Price Appraisal Expert Committee within 10 days of receiving the notice. Mao Peirong did not apply for an appraisal within the prescribed period. On January 9, 2013, the county government issued the "Decision on Compensation for Expropriation of Mao Peirong's House on State-owned Land" (Yongzheng Zhengbu [2013] No. 1), providing compensation for the residential house, interior and exterior decorations, industrial house and attachments, and losses from production and business suspension within the expropriation scope. The expropriated person chose monetary compensation, with total compensation amounting to RMB 1,842,612. Mao Peirong, Liu Jihua, and Mao Xianfeng, believing the compensation was unreasonable and the price too low, filed for administrative reconsideration with the municipal government. The reconsideration agency upheld the county government's expropriation compensation decision after review. Dissatisfied, Mao Peirong, Liu Jihua, and Mao Xianfeng filed an administrative lawsuit seeking to revoke the expropriation compensation decision.

(II) Judgment

The Jinchang Intermediate People's Court held that for the need of public utilities, the county government had the authority to organize and implement the county town's Beihaizi ecological protection and scenic area planning and construction, and had the right to expropriate the plaintiff's houses on state-owned land in accordance with the "Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land." Since the housing expropriation department and the expropriated person failed to reach a compensation agreement within the signing period specified in the expropriation compensation plan, the county government had the authority to make a compensation decision in accordance with the plan. During the expropriation compensation process, the appraisal agency was selected by the plaintiff himself; the agency had the corresponding qualifications; the review appraisal report provided a clear explanation of the omitted items raised by the plaintiff. Although the plaintiff disagreed with the appraisal review result, he did not apply for an expert appraisal to the Jinchang City Real Estate Price Appraisal Expert Committee within the prescribed period. Therefore, the county government's compensation for the plaintiff's residential house and its decorations, industrial house and its attachments, and losses from production and business suspension due to the expropriation complied with the relevant provisions of the "Several Provisions of Gansu Province on Implementing the Regulations on the Expropriation and Compensation of Houses on State-owned Land." The contested expropriation compensation decision had clear factual findings, correctly applied laws and regulations, and the procedure was lawful. The court thus rendered a judgment: dismissing the claims of the plaintiffs Mao Peirong, Liu Jihua, and Mao Xianfeng. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the parties appealed.

(III) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case is that the people's court, through exercising judicial supervision, provided strong support for expropriation and compensation actions that conform to laws and regulations. In the expropriation compensation process of this case, the expropriation department was relatively thorough and adequate in aspects such as soliciting the expropriated person's opinions on the compensation plan, selecting the appraisal agency, and determining the scope of compensation, thereby protecting the parties' right to know and participate, reflecting the principles of openness, fairness, and justice. Through the judges' explanation of the law and reasoning, the plaintiffs gradually dispelled their inner doubts and unreasonable psychological expectations. Not only did they not appeal, but shortly thereafter they reached a compensation agreement with the expropriation department, allowing the public welfare construction project to proceed smoothly. The case handling achieved good legal and social effects.

VIII. Liao Mingyao v. Longnan County People's Government — Dispute over Compulsory Demolition of House

(I) Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Liao Mingyao's house, was located in Dongshengwei Group, Longzhou Village, Longnan Town, Longnan County. In 2011, the defendant, Longnan County People's Government, approved the construction of the county's First People's Hospital, and Liao Mingyao's house was included in the demolition scope of the construction project. Regarding the demolition resettlement and compensation matters, staff of the Longnan County People's Government negotiated with Liao Mingyao multiple times, but no agreement was reached due to significant differences of opinion. On February 27, 2013, the land and planning departments of Longnan County classified part of Liao Mingyao's house as an illegal building and issued a notice for its self-demolition. In March of the same year, without complying with the relevant provisions of the "Administrative Compulsion Law" regarding advance warning, without making a compulsory enforcement decision, and without informing the party of the right to sue, the Longnan County People's Government organized relevant departments to compulsorily demolish Liao Mingyao's illegal building. At the same time, it also partially demolished legal houses within the demolition scope, rendering the house unable to function normally. Liao Mingyao, believing that the Longnan County People's Government's compulsory demolition of his house and destruction of property seriously violated his legitimate rights and interests, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Ganzhou Intermediate People's Court in July 2013, requesting that the court confirm the illegality of the county government's administrative act of demolishing his house. The Ganzhou Intermediate People's Court transferred the case to the Anyuan County People's Court for trial. After accepting the case, the Anyuan County People's Court served a copy of the complaint and a notice of burden of proof on the Longnan County People's Government within the statutory period. However, within the statutory period, the government only provided the court with relevant evidence of the administrative penalty against Liao Mingyao's illegal building, and did not provide any evidence or basis for the administrative act of compulsory demolition of the house.

(II) Judgment

The Anyuan County People's Court held that, according to Article 32, Article 43 of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 26 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the defendant bears the burden of proof for the specific administrative act it performed. It should provide the evidence for the specific administrative act performed within 10 days from the date of receipt of the copy of the complaint. If it fails to do so, the specific administrative act shall be deemed to have no evidence. In this case, the defendant, Longnan County People's Government, after receiving the copy of the complaint and the notice of burden of proof, never submitted evidence for the act of compulsory demolition of the house. Therefore, it should be determined that the defendant's administrative act of compulsorily demolishing the plaintiff's house had no evidence and was not lawful. Accordingly, in accordance with paragraph (2) of Article 57, paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the court confirmed that the Longnan County People's Government's administrative act of demolishing Liao Mingyao's house was illegal.

After this judgment took effect, Liao Mingyao filed an administrative compensation lawsuit with the court in May 2014. Through multiple mediations by the Anyuan County People's Court, Liao Mingyao and the Longnan County People's Government eventually reached a settlement agreement on the losses caused by the illegal administrative act and the demolition of his entire house. Liao Mingyao withdrew the lawsuit, and the administrative dispute was substantively resolved.

(III) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case is that it highlights the burden of proof of administrative agencies in administrative litigation and judicial authority, serving as a warning to promote administrative agencies and their staff to actively respond to lawsuits and continuously strengthen awareness of litigation, evidence, and responsibility. The law and judicial interpretations clearly specify the burden of proof of administrative agencies in litigation. Failure to provide evidence within the statutory period is deemed as no evidence for the contested administrative act, which is the legal bottom line for courts in handling such cases. In this case, the defendant demolished the plaintiff's legal house together with the illegal building during the demolition process, and subsequently failed to provide evidence in court within the statutory period to prove the legality of its act, thus had to bear the consequences of losing the case.

IX. Ye Chengsheng, Ye Chengchang, and Ye Chengfa v. Renhua County People's Government — Dispute over Compulsory Demolition of House

(I) Basic Facts

In 2009, the Renhua County People's Government (hereinafter referred to as Renhua County Government) planned and constructed the Renhua County Non-ferrous Metal Circular Economy Industrial Base, requiring the expropriation of part of the land of the Xinwei Villager Group, Xinzhuang Villager Committee, Zhoutian Town, Renhua County, Guangdong Province. The land on which the houses of Ye Chengsheng, Ye Chengchang, and Ye Chengfa (hereinafter referred to as Ye Chengsheng et al., three persons) were built was within the expropriated land scope, and were "two violation" buildings that had not obtained township planning approval or land use certificates. From August 2009 to July 2013, the Renhua County Government successively posted documents such as the "Notice on Prohibiting Rush Planting and Rush Building," "Land Expropriation Notice," "Pre-land Expropriation Notice," "A Letter to the Majority of Villagers," and "Notice on Ordering Cessation of All Illegal Building Acts" in the villager committees and groups where the expropriated land was located, informing Ye Chengsheng et al. in the form of investigation records that the land on which their houses stood was illegal land. In October 2009 and June 2013, the Renhua County Bureau of Land and Resources issued two "Notices" respectively, ordering Ye Chengfa to cease his land illegal acts. At approximately 5:00 a.m. on July 12, 2013, without issuing a notice of compulsory demolition or making a public announcement, the Renhua County Government organized personnel to compulsorily demolish the houses of Ye Chengsheng et al. Ye Chengsheng et al. then filed an administrative lawsuit with the Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, requesting confirmation that the compulsory demolition act of the Renhua County Government was illegal.

(II) Judgment

The Shaoguan Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province held that although Ye Chengsheng et al. built houses on rural collective land without government approval, which were illegal buildings, the Renhua County Government's compulsory demolition of the houses built by Ye Chengsheng et al. on the early morning of July 12, 2013, had serious procedural defects. Specifically, before carrying out the compulsory demolition, the government did not issue a compulsory demolition notice to Ye Chengsheng et al., and did not post a public notice in the villager committee and group where the demolished houses were located, requiring self-demolition within a time limit. This violated Article 34 and Article 44 of the "Administrative Compulsion Law of the People's Republic of China." Furthermore, the Renhua County Government's implementation of administrative compulsory enforcement at night violated the provision of Article 43, paragraph 1 of the "Administrative Compulsion Law of the People's Republic of China," which states that "administrative agencies shall not enforce on nights or statutory holidays." Accordingly, in accordance with Article 57 of the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the court rendered a judgment: confirming that the specific administrative act of the Renhua County Government in implementing administrative compulsory demolition of Ye Chengsheng et al.'s houses on July 12, 2013, was illegal. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the parties appealed.

(III) Typical Significance

The typical significance of this case is that it fully reflects the important function of administrative adjudication in supervising the government's lawful administration and protecting citizens' basic rights and interests. Even for the compulsory demolition of illegal buildings, the procedural requirements of the "Administrative Compulsion Law" must be strictly followed. Before demolition, the party must first be notified to self-demolish, a public notice must be posted locally, and demolition shall not be carried out at night. In this case, the defendant failed to follow these procedural requirements and was confirmed illegal by the people's court. The "Administrative Compulsion Law" has been in effect since January 1, 2012, and has been implemented for only a short time. This judgment helps promote the correct application of the Law in administrative adjudication.

X. Ye Hanxiang v. Zhuzhou City Planning Bureau of Hunan Province, Shifeng District People's Government of Zhuzhou City — Dispute over Non-performance of Statutory Duty to Demolish Illegal Buildings

(I) Basic Facts

In July 2010, Shen Fuxiang, the owner of house No. 111, Small East Gate Scattered Households, Democratic Village, Tianxin Street Dongmen Community, Shifeng District, Zhuzhou City, without the approval of the defendant, Zhuzhou City Planning Bureau, and other relevant units, demolished the old house left by his father Shen Hanru and built a new and expanded house, seriously affecting the passage and lighting of the plaintiff, Ye Hanxiang. On July 9, 2010, the plaintiff reported this to the defendant, Zhuzhou City Planning Bureau. In October 2010, the bureau investigated and surveyed Shen Fuxiang's new and expanded house, and on October 23, 2010, issued an Administrative Penalty Notice (Zhugui Fa Gao (Shifeng) Zi [2010] No. 462) to Shen Fuxiang, informing him that his building act violated Article 40 of the "Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China" and constituted illegal construction. In accordance with Article 68 of the "Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China," Shen Fuxiang was required to self-demolish without compensation within five days of receiving the notice; if not demolished within the time limit, the Shifeng District People's Government of Zhuzhou City would organize demolition. The notice was served to Shen Fuxiang himself, but he failed to demolish. From 2010 to 2013, the plaintiff, Ye Hanxiang, reported and requested the performance of the statutory duty to compulsorily demolish Shen Fuxiang's illegal building to the Tianxin Street Dongmen Community Committee of Shifeng District, the Zhuzhou City Planning Bureau, and the Shifeng District People's Government of Zhuzhou City. Despite submitting requests in the form of applications, the matter was not resolved in a timely manner. On March 8, 2013, the defendant, Zhuzhou City Planning Bureau, issued an Administrative Penalty Decision (Zhugui Fa Zi (Shi 2013) No. 6021) to Shen Fuxiang, determining that Shen Fuxiang's building act violated Article 40 of the "Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 25 of the "Measures of Hunan Province for Implementing the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China," constituting illegal construction. In accordance with Article 64 of the "Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China" and Article 51 of the "Measures of Hunan Province for Implementing the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China," Shen Fuxiang was required to self-demolish without compensation within three days of receiving the decision. If he failed to perform this decision within the time limit, in accordance with Article 68 of the "Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China," Article 54 of the "Measures of Hunan Province for Implementing the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China," and the provisions of Document Zhuzheng Fa (2008) No. 36, the Shifeng District People's Government would organize compulsory demolition. Because the defendants, Zhuzhou City Planning Bureau and Shifeng District People's Government of Zhuzhou City, failed to fully perform their statutory duty to demolish the illegal building, the plaintiff filed an administrative lawsuit with the court on June 5, 2013.

(II) Judgment

株洲市荷塘区人民法院认为，被告株洲市石峰区人民政府于2010年12月接到株洲市规划局对沈富湘株规罚告字（2010）第004号行政处罚告知书和株规罚字（石2013）第0021号行政处罚决定书后，应按照株洲市规划局的授权积极履行法定职责，组织实施强制拆除违法建设。虽然被告株洲市石峰区人民政府在履行职责中对沈富湘违法建设进行协调等工作，但未积极采取措施，其拆除违法建设工作未到位，属于不完全履行拆除违法建筑的法定职责。根据《中华人民共和国城乡规划法》第六十八条、《中华人民共和国行政诉讼法》第五十四条第三款的规定，判决被告株洲市石峰区人民政府在三个月内履行拆除沈富湘违法建设法定职责的行政行为。宣判后，各方当事人均未提出上诉。

（三）典型意义

本案典型意义在于：以违法建设相邻权人提起的行政不作为诉讼为载体，有效发挥司法能动性，督促行政机关切实充分地履行拆除违建、保障民生的法定职责。针对各地违法建设数量庞大，局部地区有所蔓延的态势，虽然《城乡规划法》规定了县级以上人民政府对违反城市规划、乡镇人民政府对违反乡村规划的违法建设有权强制拆除，但实际情况不甚理想。违法建设侵犯相邻权人合法权益难以救济成为一种普遍现象和薄弱环节，本案判决在这一问题上表明法院应有态度：即使行政机关对违建采取过一定查处措施，但如果不到位仍构成不完全履行法定职责，法院有权要求行政机关进一步履行到位。这方面审判力度需要不断加强。

The Hetang District People's Court of Zhuzhou City held that after receiving the Notice of Administrative Penalty No. 004 (2010) of Zhuzhou Urban Planning Bureau (Zhu Gui Fa Gao Zi (2010) No. 004) and the Administrative Penalty Decision No. 0021 (Shi 2013) of Zhuzhou Urban Planning Bureau (Zhu Gui Fa Zi (Shi 2013) No. 0021) against Shen Fuxiang in December 2010, the defendant, Shifeng District People's Government of Zhuzhou City, should have actively performed its statutory duties and organized the enforcement of compulsory demolition of the illegal construction in accordance with the authorization of Zhuzhou Urban Planning Bureau. Although the defendant performed coordination work and other tasks concerning Shen Fuxiang's illegal construction in the course of performing its duties, it did not actively take measures, and its work on demolishing the illegal construction was not fully carried out, which constituted a failure to fully perform its statutory duty of demolishing the illegal building. Pursuant to Article 68 of the Urban and Rural Planning Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 54, Paragraph 3 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ordered the defendant, Shifeng District People's Government of Zhuzhou City, to perform the administrative act of discharging its statutory duty to demolish Shen Fuxiang's illegal construction within three months. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the parties appealed.

(3) Typical Significance

The significance of this case as a typical example lies in: by using the action for administrative omission initiated by a neighboring rights holder of an illegal construction as a vehicle, effectively exercising judicial activism to urge administrative organs to fully and substantially perform their statutory duties of demolishing illegal constructions and safeguarding people's livelihood. In response to the situation where the number of illegal constructions is huge nationwide and has been spreading in some regions, although the Urban and Rural Planning Law has empowered people's governments at or above the county level to enforce compulsory demolition of illegal constructions that violate urban planning, and township people's governments to enforce compulsory demolition of illegal constructions that violate rural planning, the actual circumstances have been less than ideal. The infringement of neighboring rights holders' lawful rights and interests by illegal constructions, with difficulty in obtaining relief, has become a common phenomenon and a weak link. The judgment in this case indicates the attitude that courts should adopt on this issue: even if an administrative organ has taken certain investigative and punitive measures against an illegal construction, if such measures are insufficient, it still constitutes a failure to fully perform statutory duties, and the court has the authority to require the administrative organ to further perform its duties to a sufficient degree. Judicial enforcement in this regard needs to be continuously strengthened.
